input.claim_text: On 9 February 2024 I woke up to find someone had spray-painted graffiti all over our front fence and garage door overnight. It looks like it happened while we were asleep since there was nothing there when we went to bed. I haven't had anyone come out to quote on repainting or replacing the panels yet, so I don't have a cost figure at this stage. (Policyholder with NRMA home insurance.)

output.cause: graffiti sprayed on front fence and garage door during sleep

input.query: Is vandalism or malicious damage such as graffiti covered under home insurance?

output.answer:
Yes. Under the NRMA Home policy, loss or damage caused by a "deliberate or intentional act (including vandalism and a malicious act)" is covered — graffiti would fall within this category as a form of malicious/vandalism damage [NRMA Home KFS, page 1]; [NRMA Home PDS, page 13].

However, this cover is subject to important exclusions and conditions:

- **Who commits the act matters**: The policy will **not** cover damage caused by a deliberate or intentional act (including vandalism/malicious acts) committed by:
  - You;
  - Your Family;
  - anyone who normally lives in Your Home, including a tenant; or
  - anyone who enters Your Home or the Site with the consent of You, Your Family, or anyone who normally lives in Your Home [NRMA Home PDS, page 13]; [NRMA Home PDS, page 28].

- **Cover depends on policy type held**: Building damage is covered only if you have "Building" insurance (Building Plus or Building Standard), and General Contents damage is covered only if you have "Contents" insurance (Contents Plus or Contents Standard), and only while contents are inside Your Home [NRMA Home PDS, page 13].

- **Reporting requirement**: You must report the deliberate or intentional act (vandalism/malicious act) to the police and provide NRMA with the report number and details of when and where the report was made [NRMA Home PDS, page 13]; [NRMA Home PDS, page 28].

The excerpts do not specifically mention "graffiti" by name, but graffiti would reasonably fall under "vandalism" or a "malicious act" as described in these provisions.
